scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills, as requested by SH-CS (CL-01).
symptoms: CRM dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from a Jun-Jul baseline (~600/month) to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) 2026 (E-06).
Field manual-read route completion fell to 88% against a 95% contracted target over Aug-Sep 2026 across 9,200 accounts (E-01).
59% of disputed bills (1,785 of 3,025) involve ACTUAL reads rather than ESTIMATED reads (E-02).
Ticket response time (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d) remains within the 3.0d SLA despite the surge (E-04).
problem_definition_history.root_problem: CRM dispute tickets roughly doubled from a Jun-Jul baseline (~600/month) to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) 2026 (E-06). This is not explained by slow ticket handling (median response 1.6d, p90 2.8d, within the 3.0d SLA — E-04) nor by a tariff change (zero logged changes — E-03). The majority of disputed bills (59%, 1,785/3,025) involve ACTUAL, not ESTIMATED, meter reads (E-02), which caps how much the confirmed field manual-read completion shortfall (88% vs 95% target, 9,200 accounts — E-01) can explain, since that mechanism only produces estimated bills. The best-supported remaining mechanism is a defect in billing import/validation processing of actual meter reads introduced around the same period, producing incorrect bills on actual-read accounts and driving the dispute surge (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE).

challenges.rationale: ER-1: premise E-02 revised by E-12: Still shows disputed bills split 1,240 ESTIMATED vs 1,785 ACTUAL per billing-db. No longer supports that the 59% ACTUAL majority caps estimate-substitution's role as minor: E-12 shows the 1,240 ESTIMATED figure is itself fully explained by billing-side rejection of valid high-consumption AMI reads, so the defect operates through the ESTIMATED population, not the ACTUAL-majority population PR-CHAIN-2 required.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-03.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-RESPONSE-SPEED.statement: The August-September dispute surge is driven by slow/inadequate ticket response capacity, so an auto-answering AI agent targeting ticket throughput would resolve it, as SH-CS frames it.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August introduced errors that produced incorrect bills, driving disputes.

H-AMI-DATA-QUALITY.statement: Vendor-side AMI/MDMS read delivery or validation problems are feeding bad or estimated reads into billing, causing wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: Degradation in the contracted manual field meter-reading process (missed/late reads) is increasing estimate substitution and causing wrong bills.

H-SEASONAL-USAGE.statement: Bills are substantively correct and the dispute surge reflects a legitimate rise in consumption (e.g., seasonal) that customers perceive as erroneous, rather than any process defect.

H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECT.statement: Billing import validation rejects valid actual AMI reads flagged as high consumption (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), forcing estimate substitution and producing the large majority of disputed estimated bills.

H-BV17-UNIT-SCALING-DEFECT.statement: BV-17's high-consumption check compares raw register value directly against 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling "none", a candidate unit-mismatch defect that could systematically trigger false-positive high-consumption rejections of valid actual AMI reads.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Billing-db's accounts_estimated_last_cycle query shows 320 accounts received an estimated bill in the last billing cycle, spread across 40 distinct routes, but returns only account_id and route fields with no read-type, tariff, or import-status data as the NICE_TO_HAVE work item anticipated. E-11.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (vendor-side AMI Program Engineer) reports that MDMS export access for Lakeside has been provisioned as of today per vendor ticket TX-4471, addressing the acquisition blocker on DA-MDMS and the mdms-export ACCESS_PENDING state. The message says nothing about the content or quality of AMI reads, only that the export channel is now accessible.

MDMS read-event records for the 1,240 disputed-estimated accounts (matching E-02's ESTIMATED count exactly) show 1,184 had an AMI read delivered before cutoff and exported to billing but rejected by billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, while 56 had no AMI read received at all and were never exported. Together these fully account for the disputed-estimated population and indicate the dominant driver is a billing-side import rejection of valid high-consumption actual reads (forcing estimate substitution), not a vendor-side AMI delivery failure.

This confirms a billing validation rule change occurred on the exact date the dispute surge begins, specifically modifying the high-consumption check implicated in E-12's REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION outcomes.

U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED.question: Did billing import validation rules actually change around August 2026, and if so what specifically changed?
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED.decision_impact: Confirms or refutes the core defect mechanism (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE); without confirmation no remediation scope can be justified.
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED.resolution_path: Query billing-config rule-change log (DA-RULES) for entries Jul-Sep 2026 and cross-reference timing against E-02/E-06.
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED.safe_placeholder: Treat H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE as the leading but unconfirmed mechanism; keep scope strictly diagnostic (no bill adjustment) until a specific rule-change entry is found.
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED.resolution: Confirmed via E-13: rule BV-17 changed the high-consumption check (raw register value vs 12-month m3 history, no unit scaling), deployed 2026-08-01; the only other recent change, BV-09 (2026-03-02), was label-text-only and unrelated to validation logic.

U-AMI-DATA-QUALITY.question: Are vendor-side AMI/MDMS read delivery or validation problems (H-AMI-DATA-QUALITY) contributing to incorrect actual-read bills, given mdms-export access is currently pending/degraded?
U-AMI-DATA-QUALITY.decision_impact: If confirmed, implicates ORG-AMI vendor processes rather than internal billing rules, changing which organization owns remediation.
U-AMI-DATA-QUALITY.resolution_path: Request vendor-provisioned mdms-export access from ORG-AMI; retry export once tool_health for mdms-export returns to HEALTHY.
U-AMI-DATA-QUALITY.safe_placeholder: Proceed with diagnosis using DA-BILL and DA-RULES evidence only; exclude AMI-vendor causal attribution from any remediation scoping until mdms-export access is restored.
U-AMI-DATA-QUALITY.resolution: E-12 shows 1,184/1,240 disputed-estimated accounts had AMI reads delivered before cutoff and exported to billing (ruling out vendor delivery failure for the majority) but rejected by billing import validation; only 56/1,240 had no AMI read received, so vendor-side AMI delivery/validation is not the dominant driver — the defect is primarily on the billing import side.

U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-OVERLAP.question: What proportion of disputed tickets overlaps with accounts affected by the field route completion shortfall, i.e. how much does H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE actually contribute given it is capped by E-02?
U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-OVERLAP.decision_impact: Determines how much weight the field-shortfall remediation should receive relative to the billing-defect investigation.
U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-OVERLAP.resolution_path: Join DA-ROUTE incomplete-route account list against disputed-bill accounts to compute an overlap percentage.
U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-OVERLAP.safe_placeholder: Report route completion monitoring as an independent metric without attributing a specific dispute-count share to it.

U-DATA-COMPLETENESS-VALIDITY.question: Is the completeness of DA-RULES and DA-MDMS (both marked UNKNOWN at the asset level) sufficient to trust the E-12/E-13 counts as representative of the full Aug-Sep population?
U-DATA-COMPLETENESS-VALIDITY.decision_impact: If the underlying assets are materially incomplete, the 1,184/56 defect-scope counts could understate or overstate the affected population.
U-DATA-COMPLETENESS-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Check billing-config and mdms-export asset-level completeness metadata/record counts against known population totals (e.g. total accounts, total billing cycles) to confirm coverage.
U-DATA-COMPLETENESS-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Flag the E-12/E-13 derived counts as COMPLETE-at-query-level but asset-completeness-unverified; do not treat them as a final defect population without this check.

U-STAFFING-SHORTFALL-VERIFICAT.question: Is SH-FIELD's claim of being three readers short since July (E-05, non-authoritative, incentivized toward headcount increase) independently verifiable?
U-STAFFING-SHORTFALL-VERIFICAT.decision_impact: Affects attribution narrative only, not the core defect-scoping decision.
U-STAFFING-SHORTFALL-VERIFICAT.resolution_path: Request ORG-FIELD staffing roster/headcount records independent of SH-FIELD's statement.
U-STAFFING-SHORTFALL-VERIFICAT.safe_placeholder: Treat the E-05 staffing claim as unverified context; do not use it alone to justify any staffing-related action.

U-HANDOFF-MDMS-BILL-VALIDITY.question: Is the H-MDMS-BILL handoff (nightly AMI register-read export from ORG-AMI to ORG-UTIL) actually delivering and semantically valid, given delivery_status and semantic_validity are both UNKNOWN?
U-HANDOFF-MDMS-BILL-VALIDITY.decision_impact: If this handoff is failing or semantically invalid, actual-read bill errors could originate upstream of billing import, redirecting remediation toward ORG-AMI rather than the billing system.
U-HANDOFF-MDMS-BILL-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Confirm nightly export delivery logs and record counts with ORG-AMI; validate a sample payload's semantics against DA-BILL ingested reads.
U-HANDOFF-MDMS-BILL-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Treat AMI-sourced read data in DA-BILL as provisional; do not use it to confirm or rule out H-AMI-DATA-QUALITY until handoff validity is confirmed.
U-HANDOFF-MDMS-BILL-VALIDITY.resolution: E-12 shows the H-MDMS-BILL nightly export mostly delivers successfully (1,184/1,240 reads before cutoff, exported to billing) with a smaller subset (56) failing to receive any read, indicating the handoff is largely functioning but not fully reliable.

U-HANDOFF-FIELD-BILL-VALIDITY.question: Is the H-FIELD-BILL handoff (daily manual meter-read upload from ORG-FIELD to ORG-UTIL) actually delivering and semantically valid, given delivery_status and semantic_validity are both UNKNOWN?
U-HANDOFF-FIELD-BILL-VALIDITY.decision_impact: If this handoff fails intermittently, estimate-substitution counts linked to E-01 could be under- or over-stated, affecting how much weight the field-shortfall mechanism deserves.
U-HANDOFF-FIELD-BILL-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Confirm daily upload delivery logs with ORG-FIELD and validate sample manual-read payloads against DA-BILL ingested records.
U-HANDOFF-FIELD-BILL-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Treat manual-read data in DA-BILL as provisional pending handoff confirmation; do not use it to attribute dispute causation to field-read failure.

U-BV17-DEFECT-INTENT.question: Was BV-17's unit-scaling change (comparing raw register value directly vs 12-month m3 history, unit_scaling: none) an intentional policy change or an unintended unit-conversion defect, determining whether rejected reads should be reinstated/adjusted?
U-BV17-DEFECT-INTENT.decision_impact: Determines whether any future bill adjustment is warranted at all; without this, affected-account scoping must remain diagnostic only.
U-BV17-DEFECT-INTENT.resolution_path: Billing Operations Lead (SH-BILL) review of the billing-config change ticket/intent for BV-17, cross-checked against ORG-UTIL change-management records.
U-BV17-DEFECT-INTENT.safe_placeholder: Treat BV-17 as an unconfirmed defect: document and scope affected accounts (DA-BILL) for Billing Operations review, without proposing or executing any bill adjustment until intent is confirmed.

U-REJECTION-TIMING-CORRELATION.question: Did the REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION rejections in E-12 begin only after BV-17's 2026-08-01 deployment, or did similar rejections occur earlier, which would undermine attributing them to BV-17?
U-REJECTION-TIMING-CORRELATION.decision_impact: If rejections predate BV-17, the causal attribution in the root problem weakens and the defect-scope population may be mis-sized.
U-REJECTION-TIMING-CORRELATION.resolution_path: Query billing-config/mdms-export for per-record REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION rejection timestamps and compare against BV-17's 2026-08-01 deployment date.
U-REJECTION-TIMING-CORRELATION.safe_placeholder: Report the BV-17-timing correlation as unconfirmed pending per-record timestamp analysis; limit causal attribution claims to what E-12/E-13 jointly support.

A-DATA-ASSET-COMPLETENESS.statement: DA-BILL, DA-MDMS, DA-ROUTE and DA-RULES are assumed sufficiently complete for the Aug-Sep analysis despite their completeness being marked UNKNOWN.

A-BV17-CAUSAL-LINK.statement: BV-17's 2026-08-01 deployment date is causally, not merely temporally, linked to the REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION outcomes in E-12, since E-12 lacks per-record rejection timestamps to directly confirm this.

A-UNIT-SCALING-IS-DEFECT.statement: BV-17's unit_scaling "none" setting is assumed to be an unintended defect rather than intended policy, though H-BV17-UNIT-SCALING-DEFECT is only a CANDIDATE hypothesis.

A-DATA-COMPLETENESS-SUFFICIENT.statement: The E-12/E-13 query extracts (marked COMPLETE) are representative of the full population despite DA-RULES and DA-MDMS asset-level completeness being marked UNKNOWN.

problem_definition.requested_solution: Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills, as originally requested by SH-CS (CL-01).
symptoms: CRM dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from a Jun-Jul baseline (~600/month) to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) 2026 (E-06).

Of 1,240 disputed ESTIMATED bills, 1,184 correspond to AMI reads delivered before cutoff and exported to billing but rejected as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, and 56 correspond to no AMI read received at all (E-12).
Ticket response time (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d) remains within the 3.0d SLA despite the surge, ruling out slow handling as the driver (E-04).
problem_definition.root_problem: The Aug-Sep 2026 dispute-ticket surge (E-06) is caused by billing validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, which changed the high-consumption check to compare raw register value directly against 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling "none" (E-13); this rule rejects valid actual AMI reads as high-consumption during billing import, forcing estimate substitution for 1,184 accounts (plus 56 with no read received), which together fully account for the 1,240 disputed ESTIMATED bills (E-12) and drive the ticket surge.

proposal.root_problem: CRM dispute tickets roughly doubled from a Jun-Jul baseline (~600/month) to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) 2026 (E-06). This is not explained by slow ticket handling (median response 1.6d, p90 2.8d, within the 3.0d SLA — E-04) nor by a tariff change (zero logged changes — E-03). The majority of disputed bills (59%, 1,785/3,025) involve ACTUAL, not ESTIMATED, meter reads (E-02), which caps how much the confirmed field manual-read completion shortfall (88% vs 95% target, 9,200 accounts — E-01) can explain, since that mechanism only produces estimated bills. The best-supported remaining mechanism is a defect in billing import/validation processing of actual meter reads introduced around the same period, producing incorrect bills on actual-read accounts and driving the dispute surge (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE).
proposal.requested_solution: Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills, as requested by SH-CS (CL-01).
symptoms: CRM dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from a Jun-Jul baseline (~600/month) to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) 2026 (E-06).
Field manual-read route completion fell to 88% against a 95% contracted target over Aug-Sep 2026 across 9,200 accounts (E-01).
59% of disputed bills (1,785 of 3,025) involve ACTUAL reads rather than ESTIMATED reads (E-02).
Ticket response time (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d) remains within the 3.0d SLA despite the surge (E-04).
causal_chain: Around August 2026, a defect enters billing import/validation processing affecting bills built from ACTUAL (non-estimated) meter reads (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE), timing coincident with the dispute surge onset (E-06).
This defect produces incorrect bills predominantly on ACTUAL-read accounts, consistent with 59% of disputed bills (1,785/3,025) being ACTUAL rather than ESTIMATED read type (E-02).
Customers receiving these incorrect bills file CRM dispute tickets.
Monthly dispute volume rises from a Jun-Jul baseline of 610/590 to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) 2026 (E-06).
Slower ticket response (E-04: median 1.6d, p90 2.8d, within 3.0d SLA) and a tariff change (E-03: zero logged changes) are ruled out as alternative drivers.

A separate, confirmed field manual-read completion shortfall (88% vs 95% target, 9,200 accounts, E-01) independently drives some estimate-substitution, but E-02 caps this to a minority of disputes since most disputed bills are not estimated.

proposal.summary: The original request (CL-01, from SH-CS) framed the problem as slow dispute-ticket handling needing an AI auto-answer/auto-fix agent. Analysis showed this framing was wrong: response times are within SLA (E-04), and the real driver is a billing-side defect. The confirmed problem (PD-1@v2) is that billing validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 and changing the high-consumption check to compare raw register values directly against 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling="none" (E-13), causes valid actual AMI reads to be wrongly rejected as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION. This forces estimate substitution and fully explains the 1,240 disputed ESTIMATED bills (1,184 rejected + 56 no-read, E-12), which coincides with the Aug-Sep dispute surge roughly doubling from ~600/month to 1180-1260 (E-06). This was established by testing and rejecting rival hypotheses (slow response E-04, tariff change E-03, field staffing/route shortfall E-01/E-05/E-09, vendor AMI data quality) and confirming H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECT and H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE via cross-referenced evidence (E-12, E-13, E-14). The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: the DEFINE Gate gave a CONDITIONAL_PASS, and the EXECUTE-phase deliverable released is the read-only analysis/documentation of the rejection defect's scope (SD-2's release_scope: analyze_rejected_read_events on DA-MDMS), not a fix. No bill writes were made or proposed, consistent with the no-automated-bill-write constraint (K-BILLWRITE).
key_points: The initial request (CL-01) to build an auto-answering/auto-fixing AI agent was based on a root-cause framing (slow response speed) that was CONTRADICTED by evidence: ticket response time (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d) is within the 3.0d SLA (E-04), so H-RESPONSE-SPEED was REJECTED.

The confirmed root cause (H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECT, CONFIRMED; H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE, SUPPORTED) is billing rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 with unit_scaling='none' (E-13), rejecting valid high-consumption actual AMI reads during import; this fully accounts for the 1,240 disputed ESTIMATED bills (1,184 rejected-high-consumption + 56 no-read, per E-12 and account-level detail in E-14).

Alternative explanations were tested and rejected with evidence: tariff change (E-03, E-07), field staffing/route-completion shortfall (E-01, E-05, E-09 - H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE REJECTED), and vendor-side AMI data quality (H-AMI-DATA-QUALITY REJECTED, contradicted by E-12).

A later evidence revision (trigger E-12) invalidated the earlier problem definition PD-1@v1 and its linked solution design, hypotheses, assumptions and remedies (per dependency review DR-1), leading to the successor problem PD-1@v2 and solution design SD-2.
The DEFINE Gate for PD-1@v2 resulted in CONDITIONAL_PASS, with deferred items tracked as open verification obligations (VOBs).

The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, with no items placed on hold; the delivered scope is limited to read-only analysis of rejected AMI read events (SD-2 release_scope: analyze_rejected_read_events on DA-MDMS).
No automated bill writes occur or are proposed; any re-bill or credit remains a manual Billing Operations action under K-BILLWRITE's authority constraint, per the stated known limitations.

The causal link between BV-17's deployment date and the rejection outcomes is still an ACTIVE assumption (A-BV17-CAUSAL-LINK) rather than a confirmed fact, since E-12 lacks per-record rejection timestamps.
limitations_explained: VOB-U-BV17-DEFECT-INTENT is open: it is not yet determined whether BV-17's unit_scaling='none' setting is an intended policy or an unintended defect, so affected-account scoping for any bill adjustment is withheld until resolved.

VOB-U-REJECTION-TIMING-CORRELATION is open: whether REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION rejections in E-12 began only after BV-17's 2026-08-01 deployment (versus occurring earlier, which would undermine attributing them to BV-17) has not been confirmed.

VOB-R-6 is open: it is unverified whether crm-tickets (DA-TICKET) carries a reliable account identifier for high-confidence joining against the E-12 rejection population, since DA-TICKET completeness is UNKNOWN.
DA-MDMS and DA-RULES completeness are marked UNKNOWN at the asset level, limiting how representative the E-12/E-13 counts are of the full Aug-Sep population.
The solution does not execute any re-bill or credit; manual Billing Operations action remains required under K-BILLWRITE, and this release took no automated bill-write actions.
Ticket classification must avoid asserting 'defect' status until VOB-U-BV17-DEFECT-INTENT resolves; a neutral 'rejection-pattern-match' label is used in the meantime.

Three scope items remain unfinished and are blocked by open VOBs or require authority outside this release: correlating rejected reads with the BV17 deployment timeline, monitoring dispute ticket volume against DA-TICKET, and any reversion/correction of BV-17's unit-scaling parameter under Billing Operations authority.
